title: Deutsch's Algorithm
summary: One query decides whether a one-bit function is constant or balanced.
objectives: Build Deutsch's circuit with the auxiliary qubit in |−⟩ so that the oracle writes a phase
Decide with one query whether a one-bit function is constant or balanced
Explain why the circuit gives no information about f without phase kickback
mission: Call oracle(qc) once so that qubit 0 ends in |0⟩ if the hidden one-bit function f is constant and in |1⟩ if it is balanced.

prediction.question: The auxiliary qubit is in |0⟩ (not |−⟩) and the input is in |+⟩ before the query. You measure the input. What do you get?
options: Always 0 if f is constant, always 1 if it is balanced
0 or 1 with 50% each, whatever f is
prediction.explanation: The query gives (|0⟩|f(0)⟩ + |1⟩|f(1)⟩)/√2. The input is entangled with the auxiliary qubit, so measuring it returns 0 or 1 with probability 1/2 each, for any f. Without phase kickback and a final Hadamard there is no interference, and no information about f.

hints: Phase kickback needs the auxiliary qubit in |−⟩, so that the query writes (−1)^f(x) on the input.
Put the input in |+⟩ with a Hadamard before the query, and apply a Hadamard to it again after the query.
